title: Hetis: Serving LLMs in Heterogeneous GPU Clusters with Fine-grained and Dynamic Parallelism
problem: Inefficient LLM serving in heterogeneous GPU clusters due to coarse-grained and static parallelization strategies that create memory/computation mismatches and performance gaps across different model components
motivation: Production clusters increasingly use heterogeneous hardware (high-end and low-end GPUs) for cost efficiency, but existing parallelization methods fail to exploit their unique characteristics. Memory mismatches between capacity and computational power, plus performance gaps in different modules (e.g., attention vs compute-intensive ops), create bottlenecks.
method: The system dynamically breaks work into smaller pieces and assigns them to GPUs in real time based on what each GPU can handle. For the most compute-heavy operations, it spreads the work across multiple GPUs to reduce latency. For the Attention computation (which calculates how different parts of the input relate to each other), it specifically distributes the workload across lower-end GPUs by dividing it into smaller attention heads. A real-time routing system decides which GPU gets which work by weighing the time data takes to travel between GPUs, how much computation each GPU must do, and how much memory each operation requires.
key_novelty: Unlike systems that use a fixed strategy for all operations, this one dynamically adjusts how it splits work across mixed-strength GPUs based on what each part of the model actually needs.
contributions: Fine-grained parallelism framework targeting compute-intensive vs memory-intensive operations differently
Head-level Attention distribution strategy leveraging low-end GPU capabilities
Dynamic online load dispatching policy with multi-objective optimization
2.25x throughput improvement and 1.49x latency reduction vs existing systems
baselines: Existing LLM serving systems (tensor parallelism approaches)
limitations: Specific baseline systems not named; performance on different LLM architectures not detailed; heterogeneous cluster configuration specifics unclear
primary_theme: Efficient LLM Inference on Heterogeneous Hardware
